keyVerseText: And this is the number of the mighty men whom David had; Jashobeam, an Hachmonite, the chief of the captains : he lifted up his spear against three hundred slain by him at one time. an Hachmonite: or, son of Hachmoni
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun חַכְמוֹנִי (Chakmôwnîy) derives from the root חָכַם (châkam), which fundamentally means 'to be wise' or 'to act skillfully.' This root conveys not only intellectual wisdom but also practical skill and the ability to teach or instruct others. Thus, the name חַכְמוֹנִי carries the connotation of one who is wise or skillful, emphasizing a character marked by understanding and prudence beyond mere knowledge.
usageInScripture: The term חַכְמוֹנִי appears only twice in Scripture, each time referring to a person or family associated with King David. It is translated as 'an Hachmonite' or 'of Hachmoni,' indicating either a descendant or a member of a family known for wisdom or skill. This consistent usage as a proper name linked to individuals serving David highlights the name's association with those who were trusted and capable, reinforcing the implication of wisdom inherent in the term.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, the name חַכְמוֹנִי reminds believers that wisdom is a valued and God-given attribute, especially in leadership and service. The individuals bearing this name were connected to King David, a man after God's own heart, suggesting that wisdom is integral to fulfilling God's purposes. Recognizing the root meaning of wisdom in this name invites reflection on how God equips His servants with skill and insight to carry out His will. In the Christian faith, this underscores the importance of seeking divine wisdom, which is ultimately found in Christ, who is the embodiment of God's wisdom and guidance.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 11:11, the phrase 'Jashobeam, an Hachmonite' identifies this warrior as a descendant or member of the wise family of Hachmoni. This designation highlights not only his lineage but also implicitly his capability and valor, as he is described as a chief captain who single-handedly defeated three hundred enemies. The word חַכְמוֹנִי thus enriches the verse by connecting physical might with the heritage of wisdom and skill, illustrating how God’s empowerment encompasses both strength and understanding.
